name: Store-level order counts group by store_id
description: Use ONLY for store-grain metrics (store_id / store_name), e.g. which store has the most orders. Always GROUP BY store_id (store_name is not unique); store_name is a label only. Never alias store_id as hub_id. Hub questions must join orders → stores → hubs and aggregate on hubs.hub_id / hub_name; this analysis does not apply to hub month-over-month finished-order growth or any hub ranking.
sql: SELECT s.store_id, s.store_name, COUNT(DISTINCT o.order_id) AS orders FROM orders o JOIN stores s ON o.store_id = s.store_id GROUP BY s.store_id, s.store_name

name: Hub finished-order month-over-month growth via stores
description: For hub finished-order growth (e.g. February to March >20%): join orders to stores to hubs; filter order_status='FINISHED' and order_created_year=2021; COUNT(DISTINCT order_id) per hub for months 2 and 3; return hubs where march > 1.2 * february. Never treat store_id as hub_id.
sql: WITH hub_order_counts AS (SELECT h.hub_id, h.hub_name, h.hub_city, h.hub_state, COUNT(DISTINCT CASE WHEN o.order_created_month = 2 THEN o.order_id END) AS february_finished_orders, COUNT(DISTINCT CASE WHEN o.order_created_month = 3 THEN o.order_id END) AS march_finished_orders FROM orders AS o INNER JOIN stores AS s ON o.store_id = s.store_id INNER JOIN hubs AS h ON s.hub_id = h.hub_id WHERE o.order_status = 'FINISHED' AND o.order_created_year = 2021 AND o.order_created_month IN (2, 3) GROUP BY h.hub_id, h.hub_name, h.hub_city, h.hub_state) SELECT hub_id, hub_name, hub_city, hub_state, february_finished_orders, march_finished_orders, ((march_finished_orders - february_finished_orders) * 100.0 / february_finished_orders) AS percent_increase FROM hub_order_counts WHERE february_finished_orders > 0 AND ((march_finished_orders - february_finished_orders) * 100.0 / february_finished_orders) > 20 ORDER BY percent_increase DESC

name: Deduplicate DELIVERED delivery_order_id before order-grain joins
description: Use when joining deliveries into order-grain facts so multiple delivery rows do not multiply orders. Take DISTINCT delivery_order_id where delivery_status = 'DELIVERED'. Not for driver daily-delivery averages and not for hub month-over-month comparisons unless order double-counting is the issue.
sql: SELECT DISTINCT delivery_order_id FROM deliveries WHERE delivery_status = 'DELIVERED'

name: Driver delivery events counted by delivery_id
description: When counting how many deliveries a driver made, use COUNT(delivery_id) of DELIVERED rows. Do not use COUNT(DISTINCT delivery_order_id) for delivery-event counts.
sql: SELECT driver_id, delivery_order_id, COUNT(delivery_id) AS deliveries FROM deliveries WHERE delivery_status = 'DELIVERED' GROUP BY driver_id, delivery_order_id

name: Driver average daily DELIVERED counts by order_created day
description: Use only for per-driver average daily deliveries. Day grain is order_created_year/month/day; metric is COUNT(delivery_id) of DELIVERED rows; exclude NULL driver_id. Do not use for hub finished-order growth, store rankings, or month-over-month hub comparisons.
sql: SELECT d.driver_id, o.order_created_year, o.order_created_month, o.order_created_day, COUNT(d.delivery_id) AS daily_deliveries FROM deliveries d JOIN orders o ON d.delivery_order_id = o.delivery_order_id WHERE d.delivery_status = 'DELIVERED' AND d.driver_id IS NOT NULL GROUP BY d.driver_id, o.order_created_year, o.order_created_month, o.order_created_day
